During a brief chat with notebook_scribbler, I asked him to scale way, way back on the number of scans he was submitting to the sub. My reasoning for this has nothing to do with "piracy" and everything to do with the fact that I don't want this sub to become primarily known as a place to get whole-issue scans. A page or two is fine, though, especially if you're trying to spark discussion about a certain scene, writing style, or art style.

At the same time, I don't want to discourage notebook_scribbler (or anyone else) from contributing great stuff to either /v/comicbooks or Voat as a whole. It's rare these days to see someone on Voat as dedicated to posting original content to smaller subs like ours. Thankfully, notebook_scribbler has created /v/comicscans, where you can go to share any scans you may have found or created-- and I highly encourage everyone to check it out.

Once a week, I'm going to post an image on the sidebar that links to the thread of a scan that I find particularly interesting over at /v/comicscans. Or perhaps I'll base my decision off of the number of upvoats the scan has gotten-- I haven't really decided. I'll be linking to the thread rather than the scan itself in an effort to help the sub grow and encourage discussion of that particular issue. Of course, if you think the Scan of the Week should be determined some other way, *say something*!

#TL;DR

* Thanks to @notebook_scribbler for creating /v/comicscans! I encourage everyone to subscribe.

* Submit whole-issue scans to /v/comicscans rather than this sub.

* Once a week, a new **Scan of the Week** will be chosen from /v/comicscans and linked to on /v/comicbooks' sidebar. Check it out!

* You can still submit scans of a *page or two* to this sub, especially if it's to support discussion.

* *Hail Hydra*.
